_note: The text box portraits' refined pass (PortraitArt, scripts/art/portrait_art.gd: every portrait:<villager>:<mood>, the child's portrait:child:... and the generic face:<speaker>:<expression>). The same look as the figures (data/farmer_art.json, data/villager_art.json): every material of the head and shoulders (skin, hair, the top, its accent, the undershirt, the hairpin, the hat) in three tones, lit from the upper left. A pixel within `band` pixels of its part's upper-left edge takes the lit tone, within `band` of its lower-right edge the shade tone (skin by its right side only, so no shade along the chin). The black part lines become the deep tone of the material they hold, and the lines on the outer silhouette, against the background, are pulled towards `rim` by rim_mix. The eyes are drawn after the pass in `eye`, the mouth in the skin's deep tone. `materials` are the drawing's own fixed colours toned the same way: the kimono's white collar and the straw hat's cord. Our own numbers: the tones, deep and rim are the villagers' so the face in the box matches the figure in the field; band 2 because a 40 x 40 face is about twice the scale of a figure's head, so a 1 px light reads as a line, not as light.
